hints.title: Symmetric Equivalence Normalization
hints.text: Because domino orientation does not matter, represent each domino by its ordered pair min(a, b) and max(a, b).

hints.title: Two Digit Canonical Key
hints.text: Since values are between 1 and 9, a unique integer key like min(a, b) * 10 + max(a, b) fits in a small integer.

hints.title: Combinatorial Counting
hints.text: Count frequencies of each canonical key. If a key appears c times, it contributes c * (c - 1) // 2 matching pairs.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def numEquivDominoPairs(self, dominoes: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        counts = [0] * 100
        total = 0
        for a, b in dominoes:
            key = min(a, b) * 10 + max(a, b)
            total += counts[key]
            counts[key] += 1
        return total
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing all pairs of dominoes directly takes quadratic O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Normalizing each domino into a canonical integer key allows linear frequency counting in constant space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that dominoes are unordered pairs and canonicalize them.
